picks.why: Powell makes the switchgear that connects data centres to the grid, earns a 20% operating margin and a 4% FCF yield at 20x forward earnings. At 56% off its high and 33% below its 200-day, the price already discounts a lot of bad news for a business on the bottleneck the worldview rates overweight.
picks.risk: Revenue growth is only 9%, so if data-centre orders slow or the backlog shrinks, the multiple has room to fall further.

picks.why: Western Digital trades at 7.3x forward earnings with 56% revenue growth and a 41% operating margin, which prices it as if earnings are at a peak. The watchlist has no active memory name, and rising DRAM and storage pricing argues the cycle has further to run.
picks.risk: A 63% drop from the high shows how fast storage pricing can turn; a demand pause from hyperscalers would compress earnings quickly.

passed_on.reason: Good business but only a 2% FCF yield and barely off its highs; POWL gives grid exposure at a lower price.
